P1.note: make run compiles the exercise .p4 with p4c and starts bmv2 inside Mininet; edit the file and rerun.

P2.note: Hosts, switches and links come from a per-exercise topology.json; run_exercise.py builds the Mininet network from it.

P3.note: Entries in sN-runtime.json load at startup via simple_switch_CLI or P4Runtime; a separate exercise covers a Python P4Runtime controller.
P3.scope: startup load is scripted; live changes need your own controller code

P4.note: No discovery: exercises use static routes and manual ARP entries; the repo ships no LLDP or link-discovery component.

P5.note: MRI, link-monitor and ECN exercises are teaching programs to adapt; no ready per-flow collector or reporting tool.

P6.note: Ping checks by hand; exercises carry hand-written PTF tests. P4Testgen (in p4c) is the usual generator add-on.

P7.note: No graph or GUI view; interaction is the Mininet CLI (pingall, host commands).

P8.note: Scripts target bmv2 only; the repo describes no route to Tofino or other hardware.

M5.note: About 62 contributors (contributors list on repo page, 2026-10-08).

M6.note: Packet-level emulation: Mininet with bmv2 software switches.

M7.note: Not documented; the basic exercise topology has 4 hosts, 4 switches, 8 links.

M8.note: Prebuilt VirtualBox VM, build-your-own VM, or install on Ubuntu 22.04/24.04; needs enough RAM and disk.

M9.note: CLI (make run, Mininet CLI); P4Runtime/Thrift for table entries; no REST.

P1.note: p4run compiles the program with p4c and starts bmv2 nodes inside a Mininet network.

P2.note: Describe switches, hosts and links in NetworkAPI Python or JSON; IP and MAC addresses are assigned by selectable strategies.

P3.note: SimpleSwitchP4RuntimeAPI and SimpleSwitchThriftAPI expose table_add etc. to controller code; command files load entries at boot.

P4.note: No discovery mechanism documented; topology.json is generated from your own network definition at startup.

P5.note: Nothing documented for flow telemetry; you write counters or INT in P4 and poll them through the runtime APIs.

P6.note: No test generation documented; Task Scheduler only runs commands and traffic. P4Testgen or PTF are separate add-ons.

P7.note: NetworkGraph (networkx subclass) answers topology queries from topology.json; programmatic graph only, built from the definition, no GUI.
P7.scope: graph API only; not a live or GUI view

P8.note: Docs name only the behavioral-model software switch; no hardware target or Tofino path is described.

M3.note: Only tagged release is v0.0 (2018-09-09, no Python 3); master last pushed 2024-07-09, nothing newer seen.

M5.note: About 9 contributors (contributors list on repo page, 2026-10-08).

M6.note: Packet-level emulation: Mininet with bmv2 software switches and optional FRRouting nodes.

M7.note: Not documented in the pages read.

M8.note: Install script or QEMU VM (Ubuntu 20); VirtualBox VM unavailable; tested on Ubuntu 20.04/22.04; needs PI, bmv2, p4c, Mininet.

M9.note: Python API (NetworkAPI, switch runtime APIs), JSON config, p4run and Mininet-style CLI; no REST.

P1.note: Stratum lists bmv2 as a platform; the NG-SDN tutorial compiles P4 with p4c (make p4-build) and runs stratum_bmv2 in containers.
P1.scope: ONOS integration of a new program is under P4

P2.note: Mininet hosts come free, but you write the topology script; the tutorial ships a leaf-spine stratum_bmv2 example to copy.

P3.note: ONOS translates flow rules to P4Runtime writes through a pipeconf; p4runtime-sh also inserts entries directly on Stratum.
P3.locator: Writing table entries via P4Runtime shell

P4.note: ONOS finds links by LLDP; your P4 must clone packets to the controller; you write a Java pipeconf and interpreter.

P5.note: INT ships only in fabric-tna profiles (fabric-int); your own program needs its own INT code; no collector described.

P6.note: Tutorial runs hand-written PTF tests (make p4-test). P4Testgen is the usual generator add-on.
P6.locator: Tools used / P4 compilation and tests

P7.note: ONOS web GUI draws devices and links; it shows P4 devices and their pipeconf once link discovery works.
P7.scope: depends on P4 link discovery working

P8.note: Stratum runs on Tofino and Tomahawk switches via P4Runtime; the program must be retargeted from v1model to TNA.
P8.scope: Tofino discontinued by Intel (PCN Aug 2024); Stratum last release 2022-06-30; Intel BSP requests closed 2026-01-01
